scope: Pinned-source readiness for an observational macOS event-queue probe using separate Frida observer and Worker-owner scripts.

report.check: separate observer A / Worker owner B lifetime sequence
report.gate: source-readiness passed for bounded idle-worker sequence; native Darwin acceptance unrun

prior_report.correction: Earlier illustrative worker module omitted run(). Pinned bootstrap calls await w.run(); corrected source here exports run and installs RPC within it.

proven_sequence.operation: Create/load observer script A with runtime QJS in the existing session; A installs native observational replacements, retains its CModule/metrics, and calls Interceptor.flush(). Wait for host-visible armed acknowledgement.
proven_sequence.fact: A owns its GumQuickInterceptor replacement table. The underlying native Gum interceptor is process-wide.

proven_sequence.operation: Create/load separate owner script B from owner.bundle.js with runtime QJS in the same session/backend; its initial load only imports the worker URL and publishes create RPC.
proven_sequence.fact: B has its own GumQuickCore and GumQuickInterceptor tables; normal B creation reuses backend scheduler and need not itself create a fresh context.

proven_sequence.operation: Call B RPC create; it executes new Worker(workerUrl) once, then awaits worker identity RPC.
proven_sequence.fact: Worker allocates its own scheduler and fresh GMainContext in this target. With HAVE_KQUEUE, creation calls kqueue. Worker bootstrap calls exported run().

proven_sequence.operation: After B RPC completes and no worker work/messages are intentionally outstanding, unload B through the supported host script-unload API, while keeping A loaded and its replacements/CModule alive.
proven_sequence.fact: B internal interceptor flush removes B-owned entries only; native gum_interceptor_flush drains pending teardown and does not revert unrelated active replacements.

proven_sequence.operation: B successful unload destroys its context and disposes its core worker table.
proven_sequence.fact: Table destruction calls native worker terminate and unref; worker stop joins its thread, worker scheduler disposal releases its context ref, and worker core finalization releases its event-loop context ref. Last GMainContext unref closes context->kq.

proven_sequence.operation: After B unload returns, read A metrics and perform a bounded post-unload hook positive control, then revert A replacements and tear down A/session/target under existing harness.
proven_sequence.fact: No B cleanup path targets A replacement table, CModule or script. A remains able to observe native worker/context teardown, subject to actual platform replacement behavior.

exact_bundle_prerequisites.runtime: QJS explicitly for both scripts; pinned Worker tests skip non-QJS
exact_bundle_prerequisites.public_operations: Same supported session create-script/load/unload API already used by the Java harness; no private Worker implementation access.
exact_bundle_prerequisites.format: Single package marker U+1F4E6 + newline; header lists UTF-8 byte length and absolute virtual name per module; U+2704 delimiter framed by newlines precedes each module. First .js module is entrypoint. Scratch bundle encodes the exact pinned parser format used by upstream tests; no frida-compile install or rebuild is required.
exact_bundle_prerequisites.module_url: /context-worker.js is registered in B program es_assets. import.meta.url becomes file:///context-worker.js. new Worker accepts it because it resolves to an existing asset of B, not an arbitrary file on disk. A assets are not visible in B.
exact_bundle_prerequisites.worker_entry: export const url = import.meta.url; export function run() {...}. Put Worker-only initialization/RPC in run, avoiding side effects when B imports the URL.
exact_bundle_prerequisites.source_only: Bundle generated as inert diagnostic source; not loaded, compiled or executed in any target.

source_anchors.fact: Native interceptor singleton.
Each script binding obtains singleton but allocates own listener/replacement tables.
A replacement retained in that binding instance table.
Internal B interceptor flush clears only B table and then invokes native flush.
Native flush completes pending teardown, not blanket revert of active hooks.
B unload flushes its modules, destroys its context on successful core flush, then invokes unload completion callbacks.
B context destruction disposes its core.
Worker-table value destructor is gum_quick_worker_destroy.
Core dispose removes all of that core workers.
Worker destroy calls native terminate and unref.
Native worker terminate flushes and stops scheduler.
Scheduler stop joins worker thread and unrefs its main loop.
Final worker unref releases scheduler; later in same function finalizes core.
Scheduler disposal releases js_context ref.
Worker core finalization unrefs event_loop, releasing its context reference.
Last context reference closes kqueue.
Supported script source package parser registers named module assets and first .js entrypoint.
Module compile sets import.meta.url to file:// + asset name.
Worker accepts only file:// URL matching an asset in this script program.
Worker creates new scheduler/runtime in target.
Worker bootstrap imports module and calls exported run().
Pinned upstream QJS Worker RPC test uses this package/import.meta.url/exported-run pattern.

check: Verify A armed acknowledgement before B Worker creation and actual target PID identity via B Worker RPC.

A native kqueue replacement records creation and successful original result; A native close replacement records closure for that same captured descriptor during B unload, without cloaking or changing return/errno.
Wait for B unload completion, then query A metrics and verify A remains responsive; use a bounded post-unload positive control to demonstrate A replacement was not removed.
Do not infer reuse-safe general provenance from one descriptor integer or call-window correlation; retain raw native event/thread/caller metadata and exact operation boundaries.
Finally revert A replacements before disposing A CModule; complete existing target/session cleanup.

unknowns: Actual Darwin interception, kqueue variant/entrypoint coverage, original return/error preservation and closure evidence remain native gates.

Outstanding worker RPCs, queued deliveries, timers or asynchronous resources may delay worker ref release or unload. This proof covers the minimal idle worker after completed RPC, not arbitrary pending work.
GMainContext closes its kqueue at final reference release; successful B unload plus source path is not a substitute for observing actual native close.
Native close observation alone does not establish production descriptor provenance, safe FD reuse or complete action ownership.
exclusions: No remote dispatch or target execution.
No production, workflow, dependency or upstream edits.
No private Worker._impl access and no reliance on public Worker.terminate.
No broader replacement design or weakened ownership contract.

next_gate: On native macOS, observe actual queue creation and matching closure during owner-script unload while observer-script native replacements remain installed. Preserve results/errors and source-attributed native events; no descriptor cloaking or general ownership acceptance follows from source readiness.
retrieval: Decode archive.data, verify archive.sha256 and all archive members against manifest. Read report.json, retained prior-report.json correction, exact bundle sources and pinned source anchors before running the diagnostic. Original scratch paths are historical.
